subject: SOC 2 Type II — point-in-time assertion vs continuous-replay evidence timing
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightbridge-llp.com>

Cc: audit@brightbridge-llp.com

Subject: Clarify: which events count toward the report end moment?

Hi Vivek / Irene,

We're preparing the Type II testing workpapers for BrightBridge Health and need a quick clarification on how Redwood is defining the "report end moment" for the 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30 period in the PDF you provided. Two specifics: 

1) UTC vs local timestamps: our control testing looks for whether events that originate in customer-region timezones (for example, EU customers whose activity timestamps are in CET/CEST) are captured when Redwood's logs are stored in UTC. Is an event that occurs at 2026-09-30 23:59:30 local time counted as within the report period if the stored UTC timestamp is 2026-10-01 01:59:30?

2) Point-in-time assertions vs continuous replay: For some controls you attest to a point-in-time (EOD snapshot) capture, while for others there is continuous streaming/replay evidence (log retention + event replay). For partial-day migrations or backups that run during the night, are we to treat the point-in-time snapshot as inclusive up to the instant when the snapshot was taken (i.e., inclusive of the last second before the snapshot), or do you provide a rollforward/bridge mechanism that covers events that land after the snapshot instant but within the same local business day?

If you could confirm the authoritative rule Redwood follows (and whether you have a short Form bridge letter we can include in the workpapers that states your interpretation), that would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Sam Patel

BrightBridge LLP

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers below, followed by the recommended artifacts we can provide for your workpapers.

1) UTC vs local timestamps: Our internal canonical time for log storage and retention is UTC. However, when we provide evidence for SOC 2 controls that reference a customer-region "business day," we map events using the customer's declared timezone and treat the local-day cutoffs (00:00:00 local time) as the authoritative boundary for whether an event is "in period." Practically that means an event recorded in UTC at 2026-10-01 01:59:30 would be considered part of the 2026-09-30 local business day for a CET/CEST customer whose local timestamp is 2026-09-30 23:59:30.

2) Point-in-time snapshots vs continuous replay: For most system-generated snapshots we treat the snapshot instant as the point-in-time attestation (inclusive up to the snapshot timestamp). For days where we perform maintenance/migrations that cause a snapshot to be taken earlier than 23:59 local, we include an explicit rollforward policy: we keep continuous log retention and provide a reconciled rollforward manifest that shows events occurring after the snapshot instant but prior to the end of that local business day, along with reconciliation checks used in our monitoring. In other words: point-in-time snapshots are authoritative for the instant they were taken; where that instant does not align with the local-day end due to maintenance we supply rollforward evidence so that your testing can demonstrate completeness through the business day.

Artifacts we can attach today for your workpapers:
- Official SOC 2 Type II report PDF (2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30) [we will attach]
- Bridge letter template (docx) that states our timezone and rollforward policy for workpaper inclusion
- Log retention manifest for the sample dates you identify (CSV)
- Reconciliation summary showing snapshot timestamp -> rollforward last-event timestamp (CSV)

Irene, Marissa — can you attach the report and a draft bridge letter and I'll route for signature if needed? Sam, happy to hop on a 20-min call if you'd like to walk through a sample case.

Best,
